race: Formula 1 MSC Cruises Grande Prêmio de São Paulo 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to the Race Weekend Podcast, where Interlagos is back and the points math is getting spicy for the final sprint here.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: We are in Brazil with the MSC Cruises Grande Prêmio, and our top ten is built on history, fresh momentum, and a little drama.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: The stakes are huge because the title is decided, but every point still counts toward bragging rights for every team.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Quick news round up, and the biggest story is Kimi Antonelli saying his two thousand twenty seven push starts now with pressure building.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: The boy from Bologna has already switched to defending champion mode, and that is a serious mindset for next year.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: George Russell also admits he needs a deep, deep look in the mirror after his team mate took the crown, and that is honest.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Ferrari are asking if they need rules of engagement, which tells you how messy the midfield battle is for the race.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: And if you are listening, the BBC has a handy guide on how to follow the São Paulo Grand Prix from home or away, so you are ready.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Now to the big three, and I am starting with Max Verstappen because he owns this circuit and the data says so.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: He has won here, he has podiums here, and his average result over three races is better than almost anyone at this track.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the data talking, but the feel is the same. He can manage the race and still find the extra when it matters.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I put Kimi second because he is the champion, he has strong Mercedes pace, and he has a podium here this season.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: One race history is thin, but his season says he is the most complete driver in the field right now for the campaign.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Agreed, but I still trust Lando for third, because he has a win here and two podiums over three races at Interlagos.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: His Interlagos history is genuinely good, and McLaren can be quick when the setup clicks on race day, especially in the wet.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is where I part with you. I think Lando is a race day wildcard, not a sure thing for our top three.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Fair enough, but if the weather turns and the track gets slick, he is the one to watch all weekend, especially on the final lap.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Deep cut time. I am backing Isack Hadjar for seventh because Red Bull reliability and consistency matter in the top ten.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He may not flash, but he is always in the points and he can convert a strong qualifying into a result when needed.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I like Liam Lawson for eighth too, because Racing Bulls keep finding points in tricky races when it counts.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Pierre Gasly is the low confidence gamble at ninth, thanks to his Alpine form and old Interlagos history on the data.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Oscar Piastri at tenth is the other interesting one, because McLaren speed can beat poor history in a tight race.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Add Charles and Lewis to the mix, because Ferrari have pace, but their track record here is what we are watching very closely.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Charles Leclerc gets fifth for consistency and a good circuit average, while Lewis Hamilton is sixth on recent form for the weekend.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Lewis has a recent second and real Ferrari speed, but his Interlagos history is weak, so it is a nervous pick for the points.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is the balance of the weekend, and we are all ready for the drama, the speed, and the rain before lights out on Sunday.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Max Verstappen, Kimi Antonelli, Lando Norris, George Russell, Charles Leclerc, Lewis Hamilton, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, Pierre Gasly, and Oscar Piastri. See you at Interlagos, and we cannot wait.
